stories.title: AUSL All-Star Cup — Series 3 Opens Today
stories.angle: The AUSL All-Star Cup Series 3 opened today at Parkway Bank Sports Complex in Rosemont. Game 13 went to Team Coffey, who defeated Team Ricketts 4-2 on ESPNU. Game 14 was decisive: Team Kowalik rolled over Team Netz 13-5 on ESPN+, and with it, Kowalik further separated herself in the individual standings race. Six days now separate the current leader from the Series 4 finale on August 30, when the 2026 AUSL individual champion will be crowned.

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: Series 3 is here. Coffey beats Ricketts 4-2 in Game 13. Kowalik CRUSHES Netz 13-5 in Game 14. Individual standings: Kowalik 860 pts. Ricketts 604. Six days until the champion is crowned on Aug 30. This race just got more interesting. #AUSL 🥎

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Kowalik went into Series 3 with 860 individual points — nearly 260 ahead of No. 2 Ricketts. Then she wins Game 14 13-5. The individual title race is tightening in all the wrong ways for the chasers. Six days left. #AUSL 🥎

article.headline: Series 3 Opens: Coffey Wins Game 13, Kowalik Crushes Netz 13-5 in Game 14

stories.title: September 1 Countdown — 8 Days
stories.angle: Eight days until September 1 — the Class of 2028 first-contact window. But the story today expands to September 9 at 7:00 AM ET, when the in-person contact window opens. That date is when coaches can show up at practice, games, and camps for the first time. For many recruits, the September 9 experience — seeing a coach at your game — carries as much weight as the phone call. Today's angle: what to prepare for between September 1 and September 9, and why the 9-day window between the two dates matters enormously.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: 8 days to September 1. D1 coaches can call for the first time. Then Sept 9 at 7AM ET is when in-person contact opens — coaches can show up at your game. Class of 2028: prepare for both dates. They're different opportunities. #SoftballRecruiting 🥎

stories.title: Oklahoma Softball — Fall Camp Continues
stories.angle: Oklahoma's fall camp is built around the Battle Series — six intrasquad scrimmages with aggregate scoring. It's not just about conditioning. The format forces players to compete for lineup spots in game-like settings from day one. For a roster that includes Sydney Berzon (two-time All-American pitcher from LSU) and Macie Harter (.346 BA from MTSU), alongside returning Sooners and a loaded 2027 class, the fall Battle Series is the first real sorting mechanism for who plays what role in 2027.

x_posts.label: Post 4

stories.title: Texas Softball — Kavan's Senior Year Begins
stories.angle: Teagan Kavan returns for her senior season at Texas as the only player in WCWS history to win Most Outstanding Player twice. She anchors a Longhorns program that just added D1Softball National POY Isa Torres (.530 BA at FSU) and is chasing a three-peat only UCLA (1988–90) and Oklahoma (2021–23) have accomplished. Fall camp is underway. This is Kavan's last shot at a third championship — and the team around her may be the best it's ever been.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Teagan Kavan is the only player in WCWS history to win Most Outstanding Player twice. She's back for her senior year. Texas just added D1Softball POY Isa Torres (.530 BA). They went 49-12 in 2026. Three-peat or bust. #HookEm 🤘
